item.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
item.description: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized […]

item.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
item.description: NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface.  Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 […]

item.title: NASA’s Webb Shows How Supernova Dust Chronicles Star Evolution
item.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. item.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
item.description: A next-generation geodetic instrument developed by NASA, part of a network that helps measure satellites’ orbits and the planet’s shape, has debuted in Svalbard, Norway.

item.title: Summary Feedback and Interim Next Steps for NIH-Supported Research Involving Laboratory Cephalopods
item.description: In 2023, NIH sought public feedback on Proposed Guidance to Assured Institutions on Cephalopod Care and Use (NOT-OD-23-176). Since then, we have thoughtfully considered each response and shared the summary of that input on our Cephalopods in Research page.

item.title: New FAQs Available on Properly Acknowledging Foreign Collaborations and Components
item.description: In June, we shared reminders about how to properly acknowledge foreign components in NIH grant applications, progress reports, and manuscripts resulting from NIH awards (NOT-OD-26-084). Since then, we recently published new FAQs on Foreign Collaborations and Components to provide answers to some additional common questions.
